messages:
Alice K: pager alert — spike in 5xxs from v5-experimental on prod serving. Noticed at ~09:12 UTC, p50/p95 latency fine but error rate jumped from ~0.6% to ~18% over 6 mins. Keys: heavy_customer_42 and a few internal test keys. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/variants/v5-experimental

incident-bot: New incident created INC-2026-412: model-variant-error-spike (severity: high) — paging rotation: Jamie (on-call)

Jamie (on-call): on it. Paging SRE to join. Any immediate mitigation suggestions?

Raj P: First cut — throttle the top offending keys and demote traffic from v5-experimental to v4-stable. Doable with routing API + per-key quotas.

Sophie L: Confirming customer impact: ACME Corp (key heavy_customer_42) seeing ~15% 5xx, orders API affected. Two smaller tenants with intermittent failures. No broad SLA breach yet but trending.

Miguel O: repro locally shows KV cache mismatch when sequence length > 4k on v5-experimental, likely OOM fallback causing 502s. Will post logs.

Jamie (on-call): Immediate plan: 1) Apply emergency per-key quota for heavy keys. 2) Shift 100% of traffic from v5-experimental -> v4-stable for affected routes. 3) If errors persist, disable v5-experimental globally and rollback traffic to v4-stable. I will own the routing changes.

Alice K: +1. Add a circuit-breaker rule for the variant to prevent it from receiving new connections while we investigate. Also add short TTL so we can re-enable quickly if rollback unnecessary.

Raj P: Running commands now. Quota command: 
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/quotas/apply \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"key":"heavy_customer_42","rate_limit_per_min":50,"reason":"emergency-5xx-spike"}'
```

ops-bot: quota.apply success — heavy_customer_42 set to 50 req/min (applied by raj)

Jamie (on-call): Routing: shifting route group customers/production/llm -> useFilter: variant=v4-stable for keys heavy_customer_42, test keys. Command: 
```
POST /internal/routing/shift
{ "from_variant": "v5-experimental", "to_variant": "v4-stable", "key_selector": "prefix:heavy_customer_42", "mode": "immediate" }
```

ops-bot: routing.shift completed — heavy_customer_42 now routed to v4-stable (100%)

Sophie L: Observing immediate drop in 5xx for heavy_customer_42 down to ~2% within 45s. ACME Ops pinged.

Miguel O: Still seeing sporadic 502s for generic traffic on v5-experimental for non-keyed default route. Suggest disabling v5-experimental for all public traffic and moving it to isolated pool for debugging.

Jamie (on-call): Agreed. I'm going to disable the variant globally (soft-disable) so it stops receiving new requests; it should preserve in-flight tokens. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/variants/disable \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"variant":"v5-experimental","disable_mode":"soft","reason":"error-spike-1899998888"}'
```

ops-bot: variant.disable queued — v5-experimental entering soft-disable state (requested by jamie)

Alice K: Notify customer-facing teams and attach mitigations notes. Sophie, can you draft a short status message for ACME? Mention rollback to v4-stable and that we set emergency quotas.

Sophie L: Drafting: 
"We observed elevated errors on requests served by v5-experimental. We have routed your traffic to v4-stable and applied a temporary request quota to reduce retries. Our engineering team is investigating; no data loss is expected. Will update in 30 minutes."

Jamie (on-call): Disable complete: ops-bot confirms v5-experimental is drained and will not receive new traffic. Current global traffic routed to v4-stable.

ops-bot: variant.disable complete — v5-experimental drained (no new sessions), status=disabled_soft

Miguel O: Pulling logs from the drained instances: repeated OOM fallback in kernel module X at ~09:10 UTC, correlation with sequence lengths > 4k and a new attention CUDA kernel in canary build. Repro steps collected and sent to eng-runtime.

Raj P: Next steps: 1) Keep v5 disabled until eng-runtime lands a patch. 2) If we need additional capacity, spin up scaled v4-stable nodes and warm caches. 3) Create follow-up ticket ENG-ISSUE-2026-882 and link here.

Alice K: SLA/customer impact: ACME had 17 failed calls during the window, mitigated now. Recommend offering a credit if they want. Can customer success own outreach?

Sophie L: CS will own outreach and send status to ACME. Monitoring set for 30m window then 1h.

Jamie (on-call): Handoff: I'm going offline in 20 mins — handing to Raj for the watch window. Raj, please escalate to eng-runtime if we see >1% global 5xx for 10 continuous mins.

Raj P: Acknowledged. I'll take watch and own escalation. Setting PagerDuty follow-up reminder in 15m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: follow-up reminder set for INC-2026-412 in 15 minutes; assignee Raj P

Alice K: Action items (summarized): 
- [Jamie] Disable v5-experimental (done, soft-disable)
- [Raj] Apply watch and escalate to eng-runtime if threshold crossed
- [Miguel] Work with eng-runtime to reproduce and confirm fix path
- [Sophie/CS] Customer communication to ACME + offer credit as advised
- [Ops] Warm v4-stable capacity if load increases

Jamie (on-call): Thanks team. Closing the immediate mitigation steps. Will remain available for quick questions. :thumbsup:

Raj P: Leaving a note in the incident tracker and linking logs, will update timeline in INC ticket.

Sophie L: Posting customer message now.

ops-bot: monitoring.alert — 5xx rate across all variants stable at 0.9% after routing changes (below emergency threshold)

Alice K: Great work. We'll keep this thread as the source of truth. Reopen if any regressions.
